title: Collocations avanzadas y precisión léxica (make vs do, rise vs raise)
goal: Al terminar podrás elegir el verbo y el adjetivo exactos que un nativo combina con cada sustantivo (make a decision, do research, pay attention, heavy rain), distinguir pares confusos como rise/raise y lie/lay, y redactar un correo técnico sin calcos del español.

lesson.title: ¿Qué es una collocation?
lesson.html:
Una collocation es una combinación de palabras que los nativos usan juntas por costumbre, no por lógica: make a mistake, do research, heavy rain. La gramática no prohíbe do a mistake ni strong rain, pero un nativo las nota al instante. En nivel C1 ya no basta con que te entiendan: un informe o un correo con calcos se ve menos profesional, aunque cada palabra exista.

El problema para el hispanohablante es que el español usa verbos "comodín" (hacer, tomar, dar, subir) y el inglés reparte esos significados entre varios verbos. No se trata de traducir el verbo, sino de aprender el sustantivo con su verbo compañero.

lesson.title: Reglas de oro 1 y 2
lesson.html:
Regla de oro 1 — Aprende el sustantivo con su compañero

No memorices decision; memoriza make a decision. No memorices attention; memoriza pay attention to. El bloque completo es la unidad mínima de vocabulario.

Regla de oro 2 — No traduzcas los verbos comodín

Hacer, tomar, dar, tener, poner casi nunca se traducen directo. Parte siempre del sustantivo inglés y busca su verbo: hacer una pregunta → ask a question; prestar atención → pay attention; tener en cuenta → take into account.

lesson.title: Pares confusos: con o sin objeto
lesson.html:
Muchos pares difíciles se resuelven con una sola pregunta: ¿hay objeto directo? Si algo "sube solo", el verbo es intransitivo (rise). Si alguien sube algo, es transitivo (raise). Lo mismo con lie (estar tendido) y lay (colocar algo).

VerboObjetoPasadoParticipio-ingEjemplo
rise (subir, elevarse)NoroserisenrisingCosts have risen again.
raise (subir algo, plantear)SíraisedraisedraisingThey raised the budget.
arise (surgir)NoarosearisenarisingA problem arose.
lie (estar tendido)NolaylainlyingThe pipe lay in the mud.
lay (colocar, tender)SílaidlaidlayingThey laid the cable.
lie (mentir)NoliedliedlyingHe lied about the test.

Regla de oro 3 — Objeto directo → raise / lay; sin objeto → rise / lie

Prueba con "¿qué?": They raised… ¿qué? → the price. Hay respuesta: raise. Prices rose… ¿qué? → nada. Sin respuesta: rise. Al hablar y en correos es muy común go up como sinónimo menos formal de rise: Prices went up 8%.

lesson.title: Así piensa un nativo
lesson.html:
Así piensa un nativo — oye bloques, no palabras

Un nativo no aplica la regla make/do: ha oído make a mistake miles de veces y lo procesa como una sola palabra. Por eso do a mistake le "suena" mal aunque lo entienda. Tu meta es la misma: que el bloque te salga entero, sin pensar en el verbo. La vía más rápida es leer y escuchar mucho, y anotar cada bloque nuevo con su verbo, no la palabra suelta.

lesson.title: El bloque no se rompe
lesson.html:
En negativo y pregunta la collocation queda intacta; solo cambia el auxiliar. Ojo con los verbos irregulares: el pasado (rose, made, took) aparece solo en afirmativo. Con did / didn't vuelve la forma base.

EstructuraEjemplo con MAKEEjemplo con RISE
AfirmativoSujeto + verbo (pasado) + sustantivoWe made progress.Prices rose.
NegativoSujeto + didn't + verbo base + …We didn't make much progress.Prices didn't rise.
PreguntaDid + sujeto + verbo base + …?Did you make any progress?Did prices rise?
Respuesta cortaYes / No, + sujeto + did / didn't.Yes, we did.No, they didn't.

lesson.title: Detalles finos: EE. UU. vs británico
lesson.html:
Detalles finos — inglés estadounidense vs británico

  • Aumento de sueldo: a raise (EE. UU.) / a pay rise (Reino Unido). A rise in prices se usa en ambos.
  • take a decision existe en inglés británico formal; en EE. UU. lo normal es make a decision.
  • take a shower / a nap (EE. UU.) = have a shower / a nap (Reino Unido).
  • Research, progress, advice, feedback y damage son incontables: do research, nunca do a research; some feedback, nunca a feedback.
  • Algunas collocations tienen grados: a big mistake (neutral) → a serious mistake (más formal) → a grave mistake (muy formal, escrito).

examples.en: We need to make a decision by Friday, so let's take all the costs into account.
examples.es: Tenemos que tomar una decisión antes del viernes, así que tengamos en cuenta todos los costos.

examples.es: Los precios del acero subieron un 12 % en el primer trimestre.

examples.es: El cliente ha subido el presupuesto para la siguiente fase.

dialog.text: Edwin, have you had a chance to look at the new steel quotes?
Yes. Prices have risen about 9% since March, so the supplier wants to raise the unit price.
That's going to make a big difference to our margin. Did they give a reason?
They said the cost of raw materials had risen sharply. We should take that into account, but I think we can still negotiate.
Agreed. Can you do some research and find two alternative suppliers?
Sure. I'll also give you a rough estimate of the impact on the total budget.
Great. We need to make a decision by Thursday. The deadline is tight.
Understood. I'll do my best to have everything ready by Wednesday afternoon.
Perfect. And please raise any concerns early. I don't want surprises at the client meeting.
Will do. I'll make sure the numbers are double-checked.

errors.wrong: I did a mistake in the calculation.
errors.right: I made a mistake in the calculation.
errors.why: Un error es un "resultado": make a mistake.

errors.wrong: Can I make you a question?
errors.right: Can I ask you a question?
errors.why: Las preguntas se ask; "hacer" no se traduce.

errors.wrong: We must put attention to safety.
errors.right: We must pay attention to safety.
errors.why: La atención se "paga": pay attention to.

errors.right: They carried out the inspection yesterday.
errors.why: Realize = darse cuenta. "Realizar" = carry out / conduct.

errors.wrong: We did a research on coatings.
errors.right: We did some research on coatings.

errors.why: Después de didn't va la forma base.

errors.wrong: The supplier said us the price.
errors.right: The supplier told us the price.
errors.why: Tell + persona; say no lleva persona directa.

errors.wrong: There was strong rain on site.
errors.right: There was heavy rain on site.
errors.why: La lluvia es heavy; el viento es strong.

A1.prompt: Cometí un error en el cálculo de la presión.
answers: I made a mistake in the pressure calculation.
I made an error in the pressure calculation.
I made a mistake in calculating the pressure.

answers: Can I ask you a question?
May I ask you a question?
Could I ask you a question?
A1.explain: "Hacer una pregunta" = ask a question. También vale May I ask you a question?

A1.prompt: Los precios del acero subieron un 10 % el año pasado.
answers: Steel prices rose by 10% last year.
Steel prices rose 10% last year.
Steel prices went up by 10% last year.
Steel prices went up 10% last year.
The price of steel rose by 10% last year.
The price of steel rose 10% last year.
A1.explain: Los precios suben solos → rise, pasado rose. También vale went up.

answers: The supplier raised its prices.
The supplier raised their prices.
A1.explain: Hay objeto (its prices) → raise. También vale their prices.

A1.prompt: Tenemos que tomar una decisión antes del viernes.
answers: We have to make a decision before Friday.
We need to make a decision before Friday.
We have to make a decision by Friday.
We need to make a decision by Friday.

A1.prompt: Por favor, presta atención a los detalles.
answers: Please pay attention to the details.
Please pay attention to details.
They carried out the hydrostatic test yesterday.
They conducted the hydrostatic test yesterday.
They performed the hydrostatic test yesterday.
They carried out the hydrotest yesterday.
A1.explain: "Realizar una prueba" = carry out / conduct / perform. Realize sería "darse cuenta".

answers: Can you do me a favor?
Could you do me a favor?
A1.explain: "Hacer un favor" = do someone a favor. También Could you…?

A1.prompt: El plazo es ajustado, pero lo vamos a cumplir.
answers: The deadline is tight, but we're going to meet it.
The deadline is tight, but we will meet it.
It's a tight deadline, but we're going to meet it.
The deadline is tight, but we are going to meet it.
The deadline is tight, but we'll meet it.
It is a tight deadline, but we are going to meet it.
A1.explain: Plazo ajustado = tight deadline; cumplir un plazo = meet a deadline.

A1.prompt: Había mucho tráfico y llovía fuerte.
answers: There was heavy traffic, and it was raining hard.
There was heavy traffic, and it was raining heavily.
There was heavy traffic and it was raining hard.
There was a lot of traffic, and it was raining hard.
A1.explain: Tráfico y lluvia intensos = heavy. También raining heavily. Nunca strong rain.

A2.prompt: We've made a lot of progress this week.
answers: Hemos avanzado mucho esta semana.
Hemos progresado mucho esta semana.
Hemos avanzado bastante esta semana.
A2.explain: Make progress = avanzar; "hacer mucho progreso" suena forzado en español.

A2.prompt: Please take the wind load into account.
answers: Por favor, ten en cuenta la carga de viento.
Por favor, tenga en cuenta la carga de viento.
Por favor, considera la carga de viento.

A2.prompt: A problem arose during the hydrotest.
answers: Surgió un problema durante la prueba hidrostática.
Se presentó un problema durante la prueba hidrostática.
Surgió un problema en la prueba hidrostática.

A2.prompt: I strongly recommend a second inspection.
answers: Recomiendo encarecidamente una segunda inspección.
Recomiendo firmemente una segunda inspección.

A2.prompt: Lay the plates flat on the supports.
answers: Coloca las planchas planas sobre los soportes.
Apoya las planchas en posición horizontal sobre los soportes.

lines.text: Did the crew [1] the radiographic test yesterday?
Yes. We found two defects, so I'll [2] the issue at today's meeting.
Did the repair costs go up?
OK, we need to [4] that into account in the budget.

Great. Can you [6] me a favor and send it by noon?
Sure. Can we still [7] the deadline?
Yes, if the crew [8] close attention to the repair procedure.

answers: carry out

answers: raise

answers: rose

answers: take

answers: made

answers: do
meet

answers: pays

C2.prompt: Redacta un correo (7 puntos). Escribe a un cliente (Mr. Lee) un correo de 90 a 120 palabras para explicar una subida de precio. Debe incluir: (1) rise en cualquier forma, sin objeto; (2) raise con objeto; (3) una collocation con make; (4) una con do; (5) take … into account o take steps; (6) una collocation adjetivo + sustantivo (p. ej. rough estimate); (7) una collocation adverbio + adjetivo (p. ej. fully aware).
rubric: (1) rise en cualquier forma, sin objeto
(5) take … into account o take steps
(6) una collocation adjetivo + sustantivo (p. ej. rough estimate)
(7) una collocation adverbio + adjetivo (p. ej. fully aware)
C2.model:
Subject: Revised pricing for the T-210 piping package
Dear Mr. Lee,
I am writing to let you know about a change in our pricing. Over the past three months, the cost of carbon steel pipe has risen by roughly 11%. As a result, we will need to raise the unit price of the spools by 6%, effective May 1.
We are fully aware that this affects your budget, so we have taken several steps to limit the impact. We have done extensive research on alternative mills and made some changes to our cutting plan to reduce waste.
I have attached a rough estimate of the effect on the total contract value. Please let me know if you would like to discuss it on a short call.
Kind regards,
Edwin Prieto
